meta.title: "Why are you so weird?" — why your child adjusts to labels others put on them | Sila Slova
meta.description: Teach your child to separate labels from facts and not accept someone else's word as the truth about themselves. Game-based course for children aged 8–12.

hero.headline: "Why are you so weird?" — and your child is already trying to "be normal"?
hero.subheadline: No explanation, no facts — just a label. The child doesn't understand what exactly is "wrong". But already feels: something's off with me.

media.alt: A child being labelled without any explanation

pain.title: "You're just not normal" — that's not a fact, it's pressure
pain.body:
"Why are you so weird?", "you're just not like everyone else", "something's off with you". At school, in a group, in everyday conversations. The child doesn't understand what exactly is meant — but already feels uncomfortable and starts adjusting. Trying to "fix" themselves without knowing what to fix.

This isn't being oversensitive or weak. It's a natural response to vague pressure: when the person is judged rather than their action — and nothing concrete is given to work with. There's nothing to check, nothing to argue against. Just the feeling: "something is wrong with me".

The result — the child starts believing the label and changing to "be normal". They lose confidence and reshape themselves to fit expectations they don't even fully understand.

social_proof.quote: "You're just not normal" no longer makes her adjust. She's learned to ask: "What exactly is wrong?" — and when there's no answer, she understands: that's not about her.
social_proof.author: Tetyana, mum of 10-year-old Polina

faq.q: Is it a game or a learning course?
faq.a: Both at the same time. "Sila Slova" looks like a detective series, but every episode contains a hidden critical thinking lesson.

faq.q: What age is it suitable for?
faq.a: Ideal for 8–12 year olds. At this age, children are most receptive to new thinking patterns and haven't yet formed rigid biases.

faq.q: How much time is needed each day?
faq.a: 15–20 minutes per episode. Flexible schedule — your child can come back at any convenient time.

faq.q: Is registration required for the demo?
faq.a: No. The demo episode is fully open — no registration, no subscription, no personal data required.
